concepts.title: Matrix Order and Types
concepts.definition: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers arranged in rows and columns; an m x n matrix has m rows and n columns. Special types include diagonal, scalar, identity, zero, row and column matrices, and square matrices with equal rows and columns.
concepts.key_idea: Two matrices are comparable for equality only when they have the same order, and they add or subtract element-wise only when their orders match. The identity matrix acts like the number 1 in matrix multiplication.

concepts.title: Determinant of Order Two
concepts.definition: The determinant of a 2 x 2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] is the single number ad - bc obtained by cross-multiplying the leading diagonal and subtracting the cross product of the other diagonal.
concepts.key_idea: A determinant is defined only for square matrices and is written as vertical bars. A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is non-zero.

concepts.title: Determinant by Cofactor Expansion
concepts.definition: A 3 x 3 determinant expands along any row or column as a sum of entries times their cofactors, where a cofactor is the signed minor: the 2 x 2 determinant left after deleting the entry's row and column, with sign given by the checkerboard pattern.
concepts.formula: det = a * (e * i - f * h) - b * (d * i - f * g) + c * (d * h - e * g)
concepts.key_idea: Choosing the row or column with the most zeros minimises the work, since a zero entry contributes nothing regardless of its cofactor.
question_patterns: Evaluate the determinant [[{a}, {b}, {c}], [{d}, {e}, {f}], [{g}, {h}, {i}]].

solution_steps.compute: det = a * m11 - b * m12 + c * m13

concepts.title: Matrix Product Entries
concepts.definition: The product AB is defined when A has as many columns as B has rows, and the entry in row i column j of AB is the sum of products of row i of A with column j of B. For 2 x 2 matrices the top-left entry is a11*b11 + a12*b21.
concepts.key_idea: Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative: AB differs from BA. Each entry costs a row-times-column inner product, which is why order matters in the computation itself.
question_patterns: Compute the entry in the first row and first column of AB for the given 2 x 2 matrices.

If A is 2 x 3 and B is 3 x 2, what is the order of AB?

concepts.title: Area of Triangle by Determinant
concepts.definition: The area of a triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3) equals half the absolute value of the determinant x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2). The three points are collinear exactly when this expression is zero.
concepts.key_idea: A zero signed area means the three points lie on one line, so the same determinant doubles as a collinearity test.
question_patterns: Find the area of the triangle with vertices ({x1}, {y1}), ({x2}, {y2}) and ({x3}, {y3}).

concepts.title: Symmetric and Skew Symmetric Matrices
concepts.definition: A square matrix A is symmetric when its transpose equals itself (A' = A), and skew symmetric when its transpose equals its negative (A' = -A). Every skew symmetric matrix has zeros on its main diagonal.
concepts.key_idea: For any square matrix, A + A' is symmetric and A - A' is skew symmetric, which decomposes A into a symmetric part plus a skew symmetric part. A' means the transpose: rows and columns interchanged.

concepts.title: Solving Systems by Cramer and Inverse Methods
concepts.definition: A system of linear equations with square coefficient matrix A and column vector of constants B solves as X = A-inverse B when the determinant of A is non-zero. Cramer's rule gives each unknown as the ratio of two determinants: replace the unknown's column in A by B for the numerator determinant, and divide by the determinant of A.
concepts.key_idea: The system has a unique solution exactly when the determinant of the coefficient matrix is non-zero; a zero determinant means either no solution or infinitely many, and the row reduction method distinguishes those cases.

concepts.title: Leontief Input-Output Model
concepts.definition: In the two-sector Leontief input-output model, each industry consumes a fraction of another industry's output to produce its own. Writing A for the input-coefficient matrix and D for final demand, the gross output vector solves X = (I - A) inverse D, where I is the identity.
concepts.key_idea: The model computes how much each sector must produce in total so that both internal consumption and the final demand are met; production is viable only when the column sums of the technology matrix stay below 1.

worked_examples.q: Find the determinant of [[3, 4], [2, 5]] and state whether the matrix is invertible.
worked_examples.a: det = 3 x 5 - 4 x 2 = 15 - 8 = 7. The determinant is non-zero, so the matrix has an inverse.

worked_examples.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (4, 6) and (5, 1).
worked_examples.a: Twice the area = 1 x (6 - 1) + 4 x (1 - 2) + 5 x (2 - 6) = 5 - 4 - 20 = -19. Area = |-19| / 2 = 9.5 square units. The non-zero value also confirms the points are not collinear.
